title: Dictionaries and Sets
summary: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> for lookups by key - adding, reading safely with TryGetValue, updating, counting and grouping, iterating key-value pairs - and HashSet<T> for unique values and set operations, with case-insensitive keys, sorted variants and queues and stacks.

cards.q: What happens when you read dict["missing"]?
cards.a:
It throws KeyNotFoundException; use TryGetValue or GetValueOrDefault instead

Reading a missing key with the indexer throws. Returning the default is what `GetValueOrDefault` does, and only writing `dict["missing"] = v` adds a key.

cards.q: What does HashSet.Add return for a value already in the set?
cards.a:
false, and the set is unchanged

A set never holds duplicates, so `Add` reports false and changes nothing. Throwing for a duplicate is what `Dictionary.Add` does.

cards.q: Which collection should store "has this user name been taken?" for a million names?
cards.a:
HashSet<string>

HashSet.Contains takes about the same time however many items there are; a list checks every item.
